transcript:
[00:00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into how NimbleDocs is currently doing retrieval and what you're trying to optimize for.
[00:00:12] Priya (NimbleDocs): Hi, I'm Priya, head of search. Thanks, Sofia. We've got Evan, our platform eng, and Ruth from data science.
[00:00:18] Evan (NimbleDocs): Hey.
[00:00:20] Ruth (NimbleDocs): Hi all.
[00:00:23] James (Redwood SE): Hey team, James here - I focus on latency and scale. A couple clarifying q's then we can go into details.
[00:00:30] Priya: Great. To frame the problem: we run a knowledge base search for enterprise docs. Right now our system uses BM25 for recall then a dense reranker using faiss for ANN. We use 1536-d embeddings from a commercial encoder.
[00:00:48] Sofia: Cool. Is that fully managed or self-hosted?
[00:00:51] Priya: Self-hosted. We run the vector index on a cluster of machines - it's a mix of Milvus and some custom shards backed by S3 for vectors. It's... getting expensive and operationally heavy.
[00:01:05] James: When you say expensive, are you seeing cost spikes or operational headaches?
[00:01:09] Priya: Both. The cold-starts, re-indexing windows, and the need to scale up for batch re-embeds are killing our ops team. Also inference cost on the embedding encoder is large.
[00:01:20] Ruth: Also model drift. We push weekly re-embeds; that's a heavy job.
[00:01:24] Evan: From infra, our requirements: PII redaction for some doc sets, VPC-only access, and consistent throughput during business hours.
[00:01:33] James: Good color. What throughput are you targeting?
[00:01:36] Priya: For our internal SLAs we target ~120 QPS peak for retrieval and wants tail latency under 200 ms for the rerank stage.
[00:01:45] Sofia: 120 QPS is helpful. Are those 120 QPS pure vector nearest neighbor lookups or end-to-end with reranker?
[00:01:51] Priya: End-to-end. So BM25+vector candidate generation then re-rank with a small transformer. Usually 10-20 candidates.
[00:02:00] James: Ok. We typically recommend Continuous Batching + KV cache for the autoregressive rerank if you use Redwood for the reranker, and for vector lookups we support smart routing — e.g., route to a Hosted lightweight index for tail queries and Dedicated for sustained throughput.
[00:02:16] Evan: We need to understand networking: V P C peering vs private deployment. For compliance we prefer private deployment inside our VPC or on-prem. How does Redwood Private work re: KMS and audit logs?
[00:02:27] Sofia: For Private we provide control-plane connectivity options and a customer-managed control plane in your VPC. Key management can be integrated with your KMS/HSM and we surface audit logs to your log collector. There are a few packaging options — on-prem appliance vs VPC-managed — James can share more details.
[00:02:42] James: Yes, we support KMS integration, SAML SSO, RBAC, and long-term audit retention as an add-on. One caveat: on-prem tends to have longer lead time for setup, whereas Dedicated (hosted within our infra but isolated GPUs) can be faster to start.
[00:02:58] Ruth: If we did Dedicated, can we still do VPC egress controls so our traffic never leaves our cloud region?
[00:03:04] James: Yes, Dedicated supports region pinning and private network connections; we can use V P C peering or private link. There are some configs for egress NAT depending on your cloud.
[00:03:13] Priya: Performance impact question: if we move to 1024-d embeddings instead of 1536, what are typical latency/cost changes?
[00:03:21] James: Dropping dims usually reduces index size ~33% and ANN query time improves because L2/inner-product ops are cheaper, plus smaller KV cache for rerank. But there's a relevance tradeoff. We typically recommend running an A/B on a held-out query set — James: we'll help with offline eval.
[00:03:37] Sofia: Right — and Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching settings to hit your cost/latency sweet spot.
[00:03:44] Evan: Can Redwood integrate with our existing vector store? We don't want a full migration immediately.
[00:03:49] Sofia: Yes. Many customers keep their current vector DB and use Redwood as the reranker and embedding service or as a hybrid setup. We support connectors for popular vector DBs and can do fallback to your local index.
[00:04:00] Priya: So fallback routing — like if Dedicated is saturated or we have region failover, would it route to smaller hosted model or local store?
[00:04:08] James: Exactly. You can specify routing policies: prefer low-latency region, then Dedicated, then a cost tier. For rerank we can fallback to a smaller model or to a heuristic score if model capacity is unavailable.
[00:04:18] Priya: Sounds good. On security, SOC 2 is a must for our enterprise customers. Do you have SOC 2 and ISO?
[00:04:24] Sofia: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO reports we can share — we'll attach the SOC 2 pack. For Private deployments we map controls to your audit process.
[00:04:33] Evan: Data residency: some customers require EU-only host. Can Redwood guarantee region residency for Dedicated?
[00:04:39] James: Yes, Dedicated and Private can be region-locked. Hosted API is multi-region but you can pin to region for data locality.
[00:04:46] Ruth: For the reranker model, are you recommending we push rerank into Redwood or keep our small transformer in-house?
[00:04:52] James: Depends on control vs ops. If you want full control over weights and auditing, keep in-house and use Redwood just for candidate gen and scoring. If you want simplified ops and consistent latency, hosting rerank with Redwood on Dedicated GPUs reduces ops burden and gives automatic batching.
[00:05:06] Priya: Latency numbers: you mentioned 200 ms tail earlier. Is that realistic for a rerank on 10 candidates at 120 QPS?
[00:05:13] James: With Dedicated and optimized batching we believe you can hit <150 ms p50 and keep p95 near 200ms for that footprint. We'll need to benchmark with your actual payloads — tokenization and candidate size matter.
[00:05:27] Evan: What about caching — prefix or KV cache — could that reduce costs for repeated queries?
[00:05:31] James: Yes, prefix/KV caching yields big savings for hot queries. If your user behavior has repetition (same doc titles or common queries), caching reduces token compute. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching + KV cache invalidation policies.
[00:05:45] Priya: Operational question: do you support matrix of models? Eg we want to try 1536 encoder + heavy rerank model for high-value customers, and a lower-cost 1024/quantized option for standard users.
[00:05:56] Sofia: Absolutely, you can maintain multiple model variants and rollouts — canary and A/B. Console shows token-level cost so you can route by customer tier.
[00:06:05] Ruth: How long to onboard a pilot for, say, 10k docs and a 2-week smoke test?
[00:06:10] James: For Dedicated it's typically 2-3 weeks to get reserved capacity and set up connectors; Private longer. For Hosted pilot it's fastest — we can do a Hosted pilot in a few days if you can share sample data and credentials.
[00:06:22] Evan: What about SSO for our team?
[00:06:25] Sofia: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning.
[00:06:28] Priya: Cost: rough order of magnitude for Dedicated to hit 120 QPS rerank workloads?
[00:06:34] Sofia: We'll send an estimate — depends on model size and batching. Ballpark: a Dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling to handle 120 QPS could be in the low tens of thousands per month, but we'll provide a tailored worksheet.
[00:06:46] Priya: Ok. For the pilot success criteria: we want p95 under 250ms end-to-end, CPU ops reduced for our infra, and a 20% reduction in cost per query.
[00:06:57] James: Noted. We'll propose a benchmark plan with those KPIs.
[00:07:01] Ruth: Any limitations on vector dims or quantization?
[00:07:05] James: We support typical dims up to 4096 but most customers are 768-2048. Quantized indexes and int8/4-bit quantization are supported in certain configs — there's a tradeoff in recall. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization based on your eval set.
[00:07:20] Priya: Great. A few misc items: can we run a small AB test of 1024 vs 1536 for a subset of queries?
[00:07:26] Sofia: Yes, absolutely. We'll help set up the eval harness and metrics for precision@k and business metrics.
[00:07:32] Evan: For the connector, we want to avoid syncing entire index initially. Is there a streaming ingestion option?
[00:07:37] James: Yes, streaming ingestion and incremental syncs are supported; you can point to S3 or event streams. We can also do a one-time snapshot ingest for the pilot.
[00:07:46] Priya: Timeline wise, we'd like to run a 4-week pilot starting late May. Is that feasible?
[00:07:51] Sofia: Yes, if we kick off next week with sample data and sign a pilot NDA/PO we'll aim for late-May start.
[00:07:58] Evan: One last thing: network egress and NAT — if we do Private, we need to keep everything internal.
[00:08:04] James: Understood — Private can be fully air-gapped with customer-managed egress; we'll document network diagrams as part of the security pack.
[00:08:13] Sofia: Ok wrapping up — I'll share the pricing worksheet, SOC 2 pack, and a sample pilot agreement. James will share the perf checklist. Evan, Priya, Ruth any final asks?
[00:08:23] Priya: Please include example query sets for benchmarking and a template for success metrics.
[00:08:28] Ruth: Also, a short note on tokenization differences if we host rerank models in Redwood vs local.
[00:08:33] Evan: ACL and S3 access checklist for the connector.
[00:08:36] Sofia: Got it. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for next week to finalize scope.
[00:08:43] Priya: Thanks.
[00:08:44] Ruth: Thanks all.
[00:08:45] James: Thanks.
